source_text: Οὐ γὰρ μωραίνομεν, ἄνδρες Ἕλληνες, οὐδὲ λήρους ἀπαγγέλλομεν, θεὸν ἐν ἀνθρώπου μορφῇ γεγονέναι καταγγέλλοντες. Οἱ λοιδοροῦντες ἡμᾶς συγκρίνατε τοὺς μύθους ὑμῶν τοῖς ἡμετέροις διηγήμασι. Δηΐφοβος, ὥς φασιν, ἦν ἡ Ἀθηνᾶ διὰ τὸν Ἕκτορα, καὶ χάριν Ἀδμήτου Φοῖβος ἀκειρεκόμης τὰς εἰλίποδας βοῦς ἐποίμαινε, καὶ πρεσβύτις ἀφικνεῖται πρὸς τὴν Σεμέλην ἡ τοῦ Διὸς γαμετή.Τοιαῦτα δὲ μελετῶντες πῶς ἡμᾶς διαγελᾶτε; Τέθνηκεν ὑμῶν ὁ Ἀσκληπιός, καὶ ὁ τὰς πεντήκοντα παρθένους μιᾷ νυκτὶ Θεσπιάσι διακορεύσας βορᾷ πυρὸς ἑαυτὸν παραδοὺς οἴχεται. Προμηθεὺς τῷ Καυκάσῳ προσαρτηθεὶς τιμωρίαν χάριν τῆς εἰς ἀνθρώπους εὐεργεσίας ὑπήνεγκεν. Φθονερὸς ὁ Ζεὺς καθ᾿ ὑμᾶς, καὶ κρύπτει τὸν ὄνειρον τοῖς ἀνθρώποις βουλόμενος ἀπόλλυσθαι. Διόπερ ἀποβλέψαντες πρὸς τὰ οἰκεῖα ἀπομνημονεύματα κἄν ὡς ὁμοίως μυθολογοῦντας ἀποδέξασθε. Καὶ ἡμεῖς μὲν οὐκ ἀφραίνομεν, φλήναφα δὲ τὰ ὑμέτερα. Γένεσιν ἄν λέγητε θεῶν, καὶ θνητοὺς αὐτοὺς ἀποφανεῖσθε. Διὰ τί γὰρ οὐ κύει νῦν ἡ Ἥρα; Πότερον γεγήρακεν, ἤ τοῦ μηνύσαντος ὑμῖν ἀπορεῖται; Πείσθητέ μοι νῦν, ὦ ἄνδρες Ἕλληνες, μηδὲ τοὺς μύθους μηδὲ τοὺς θεοὺς ὑμῶν ἀλληγορήσητε. Κἄν γὰρ τοῦτο πράττειν ἐπιχειρήσητε, θεότης ἡ καθ᾿ ὑμᾶς ἀνῄρηται καὶ ὑφ᾿ ὑμῶν· οἱ γὰρ τοιοῦτοι παρ᾿ ὑμῖν ὄντες οἱ δαίμονες, ὁποῖοι καὶ λέγονται, φαῦλοι τὸν τρόπον εἰσίν, ἢ μεταγενόμενοι πρὸς τὸ φυσικώτερον οὔκ εἰσιν οἷοι καὶ λέγονται. Σέβειν δὲ τῶν στοιχείων τὴν ὑπόστασιν οὔτ᾿ ἂν πεισθείην, οὔτ᾿ ἂν πείσαιμι τὸν πλησίον.Καὶ Μητρόδωρος δὲ ὁ Λαμψακηνὸς ἐν τῷ περὶ Ὁμήρου λίαν εὐήθως διείλεκται, πάντα εἰς ἀλληγορίαν μετάγων. Οὔτε γὰρ Ἥραν οὔτε Ἀθηνᾶν οὔτε Δία τοῦτ᾿ εἶναί φησιν ὅπερ οἱ τοὺς περιβόλους αὐτοῖς καὶ τεμένη καθιδρύσαντες νομίζουσι, φύσεως δὲ ὑποστάσεις καὶ στοιχείων διακοσμήσεις. Καὶ τὸν Ἕκτορα δὲ καὶ τὸν Ἀχιλλέα δηλαδὴ καὶ τὸν Ἀγαμέμνονα καὶ πάντας ἁπαξαπλῶς Ἕλληνάς τε καὶ βαρβάρους σὺν τῇ Ἑλένῃ καὶ τῷ Πάριδι, τῆς αὐτῆς φύσεως ὑπάρχοντας, χάριν οἰκονομίας ἐρεῖτε παρεισῆχθαι, οὐδενὸς ὄντος τῶν προειρημένων ἀνθρώπων. Ταῦτα δὲ ἡμεῖς προετείναμεν ὥσπερ ἐπὶ ὑποθέσεως· τὴν γὰρ ἡμετέραν περὶ τοῦ θεοῦ κατάληψιν οὐδὲ συγκρίνειν ὅσιον τοῖς εἰς ὕλην καὶ βόρβορον κυλινδουμένοις.
pass_a_gloss: For we do not speak foolishly, men of Greece, nor do we announce idle tales, proclaiming God to have come into being in human form. You who revile us, compare your myths to our stories. Deiphobus, as they say, was loved by Athena on account of Hector, and Phoebus, unmindful of Admetus, pastured the curl-horned oxen, and an old woman came to Semele, the bride of Zeus. And practicing such things, how do you laugh at us? Your Asclepius died, and the one who corrupted the fifty virgins of the Thespians in one night, having given himself to the fire, departed. Prometheus, having been bound to the Caucasus, endured punishment on account of the benefit to men. Zeus is envious towards you, and hides the dream from men, wishing them to perish. Therefore, looking to your own records, even if you receive us as speaking similarly in myths. And we do not speak foolishly, but we despise your things. You might say the genesis of the gods, and you will declare them to be mortal. Why does Hera not conceive now? Has she grown old, or is she at a loss because the one who announced it to you is absent? Be persuaded by me now, men of Greece, and do not allegorize your myths or your gods. For even if you attempt to do this, the divinity according to you has been lifted and by you; for the such-like beings among you, who are called demons, are of a base character, or they are not what they are said to be, having come later to what is more natural. But I would not be persuaded to reverence the substance of the elements, nor would I persuade the one next to me. And Metrodorus of Lampsacus also, in his work on Homer, has spoken very well, transferring everything to allegory. For he says that neither Hera nor Athena nor Zeus is what those who have built temples and precincts around them think, but rather they are substances of nature and adornments of elements. And he will say that Hector and Achilles and Agamemnon and all the Greeks and barbarians, along with Helen and Paris, being of the same nature, were introduced for the sake of economy, none of the aforementioned people being real. But we have proposed these things as if on a hypothesis; for it is not holy to compare our conception of God to those who are rolled in matter and mud.

pass_b_english: We Greeks are not speaking foolishly, nor are we peddling idle tales by proclaiming that God has come into being in human form. You who revile us, compare your own myths with our accounts. Take Deiphobus: they say Athena loved him for Hector's sake. Phoebus, with his unshorn locks, tended Admetus' curling-horned cattle. An old woman approached Semele, Zeus's bride. Practicing such stories, how can you laugh at us? Your Asclepius died. The man who deflowered the fifty Thespian virgins in a single night threw himself into the fire and perished. Prometheus, bound to the Caucasus, suffered punishment for benefiting humanity. Zeus is jealous toward you; he withholds the dream from mortals, wanting them to perish. So examine your own records and grant us the same hearing, even if you class our teaching as myth. We are not foolish; we despise your fables. You claim a genesis for the gods, yet you declare them mortal. Why does Hera not conceive now? Has she grown old, or is she at a loss because the one who announced it to you is gone? Be persuaded, men of Greece: do not allegorize your myths or your gods. Even if you attempt it, the divinity you worship is abolished by your own hand; for the beings you call demons are base in character, or, if later transformed into something more natural, they are not what they are said to be. I would not be persuaded to revere the substance of the elements, nor would I persuade anyone else. Metrodorus of Lampsacus, in his work on Homer, has argued quite innocently, turning everything into allegory. He says that neither Hera nor Athena nor Zeus is what those who built temples and precincts for them imagine, but rather substances of nature and adornments of the elements. He would also say that Hector, Achilles, Agamemnon, and all the Greeks and barbarians together with Helen and Paris—being of the same nature—were introduced for the sake of a scheme, none of those people having actually existed. We have put these points forward only by way of hypothesis; for it is not right to compare our conception of God with those who are rolled in matter and mud.

review.notes: Pass A fails on the translation of 'ἀκειρεκόμης' (unshorn/unhaircut) as 'unmindful' (which would be 'ἀμελῶν/ἀμελησῶν'). Pass B correctly translates it as 'unshorn locks', but Pass A is a required component of the fidelity check. Additionally, Pass A translates 'ἀποβλέψαντες πρὸς τὰ οἰκεῖα ἀπομνημονεύματα' as 'looking to your own records', whereas the Greek 'ἀποβλέψαντες' (casting aside/rejecting) suggests a different sense, though this is a matter of interpretation. The primary failure is the mistranslation of 'ἀκειρεκόμης' in Pass A.
